draft.title: Corresponding and alternate angles
card: A transversal is a line that crosses two or more other lines. Here the two lines it crosses are parallel, which means they stay the same distance apart and never meet.
Corresponding
angles in matching positions at the two crossings, forming an F shape. They are equal.
Alternate
angles on opposite sides of the transversal and between the parallel lines, forming a Z shape. They are equal.
Example: one angle is 65°. The corresponding angle is 65°. The alternate angle is also 65°. These rules only work when the lines are parallel.
draft.remember: Parallel lines: F shape angles are equal and Z shape angles are equal.

a.q: A transversal crosses two parallel lines. One angle at the top crossing is 70°. What is the alternate angle at the lower crossing?
a.why: Alternate angles (Z shape) between parallel lines are equal, so the angle is 70°. 110° is 180° − 70°, which is not the rule for alternate angles.
a.clue: Trace a Z shape. Are the two angles equal or different?

b.q: Two parallel fence rails are crossed by a diagonal brace. At the top rail, the angle is 48°. What is the corresponding angle at the bottom rail?
b.why: Corresponding angles (F shape) between parallel lines are equal, so the angle is 48°. 132° comes from subtracting from 180°, which is a different rule.
b.clue: Corresponding angles sit in matching positions, like an F.

problems.detail: The why says corresponding angles are 'between parallel lines', but they are not both between the lines: one sits between them and one sits outside. This clashes with the card, which keeps 'between the parallel lines' for alternate angles only. Reword to 'when a transversal crosses parallel lines'.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer (70° and 48°). The only issue is that why (b) says corresponding angles lie 'between' the parallel lines, which is wrong and blurs the card's distinction from alternate angles.
